requirements.evidence: Most of the contract is there: models/relations/scopes (app/Models/Entity.php, EntityMembership.php), UserRole::manageable(), policies, factories with states, routes onboarding/entity.switcher/entity.pick/entity.dashboard (routes/web.php:23-67), the current_entity alias (bootstrap/app.php:19-21), the middleware dispatch 0/1/>1 plus a 403 (app/Http/Middleware/CurrentEntity.php:26-46), slug retry through the overridable uniqueSlug() (CreateEntity.php:31-57), the audit logs, the switcher markup and the navbar link. The problem is the owner constraint, which uses `ALTER TABLE entity_memberships ADD COLUMN owner_seq TINYINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:31-33). SQLite does not allow ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN to add a STORED generated column (only VIRTUAL), so the migration fails on SQLite. That breaks the explicit 'portably on SQLite and MariaDB' requirement and every RefreshDatabase test on SQLite. Smaller gap: /home with a single membership whose entity is soft-deleted dereferences a null `$entity` (routes/web.php:31-35).

conventions.evidence: The good parts: #[Validate] + $this->validate() in CreateEntity.php:19-25, policies in app/Policies, deliberate $fillable, reversible down(), docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG updated, and Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware for the custom middleware (AppServiceProvider.php:42). The deviations: the domain write (create the entity and its owner membership) sits inline in the Livewire component instead of an app/Actions class (CreateEntity.php:36-48). The migration uses raw DB::statement SQL instead of Blueprint's storedAs() inside Schema::create. The /home, switcher and pick logic lives in route closures (routes/web.php:23-63).

security.evidence: submit() validates and calls $this->authorize('create', Entity::class) (CreateEntity.php:25-27). The role is hard-coded to UserRole::Owner, not taken from client input (CreateEntity.php:44). The Dashboard mount authorizes view (Dashboard.php:17). entity.pick checks can('view') before touching the session (routes/web.php:53). The middleware aborts 403 for a session entity the user is not a member of. All output is escaped with {{ }}. Only gap: the entity-creation action has no rate limit.

tests.evidence: The tests are broad and meaningful: policies for every role (EntityPoliciesTest.php), DB constraints (EntityMembershipTest.php:37-69), the insert-time slug race through a subclass overriding uniqueSlug (EntityOnboardingTest.php:13-23,121-135), the tenant session/home/switcher/pick/navbar paths and 403 cases (EntityTenantSessionTest.php), and the audit logs mocked. Missing: the Livewire unauthorized-call and tamper tests the policy requires for CreateEntity::submit. 'the creator cannot choose a different role' (EntityOnboardingTest.php:91-102) tampers nothing. The suite also depends on the migration, which fails on SQLite.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean: small policies with private roleFor()/isManager() helpers and a simple bounded retry loop. There is some duplication: the 0/1/>1 membership dispatch is written twice, in CurrentEntity.php:26-40 and routes/web.php:24-39. Laravel's storedAs() would have been simpler than raw SQL.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, sibling style is consistent, and the generated-column trick (migration:28-30) and the retry (CreateEntity.php:52-53) have useful comments. There is no debug code. The route closures in web.php are getting long.

scope.evidence: The diff adds two unrelated CI workflows: .github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml (65 lines, deploy secrets) and .github/workflows/tests.yml. It also makes a cosmetic, unrelated change: `->middleware(['throttle:6,1'])` (routes/web.php:92). Everything else serves the task, and no out-of-scope features (members/settings pages, locale middleware) were built.

issues.explanation: SQLite rejects ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN for a STORED generated column, so the migration (and every test on SQLite) fails; the column should be declared inside Schema::create, e.g. ->nullable()->storedAs(...).
Creating the entity and its owner membership is a domain write and should be an app/Actions class (e.g. CreateEntity action) that authorizes inside, as the conventions require.
The diff adds new CI/deploy workflows (including secret wiring) that have nothing to do with the entity task.
There is no unauthorized-call (guest) test or real tamper test for CreateEntity::submit as the Livewire policy requires; the 'cannot choose a different role' test tampers nothing.
If the user's only membership belongs to a soft-deleted entity, `$entity` is null and getKey() throws, giving a 500 instead of a clean dispatch.
The 0/1/>1 membership dispatch is written twice instead of shared.
The migration uses raw SQL statements where Blueprint already offers storedAs() and a named unique() index.
The entity-creation action is not rate-limited, so one user can create entities without limit.
The layout runs a count query on every page render; acceptable but worth noting.
The unrelated change of `'throttle:6,1'` to `['throttle:6,1']` is churn.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership model, policies, onboarding with slug retry, the tenant-session middleware, the switcher, the dashboard and the navbar link, with broad tests and updated docs. But the single-owner generated column is added with ALTER TABLE ... STORED, which SQLite rejects, so the required portable constraint (and the test suite on SQLite) breaks. It also skips the Actions convention for the domain write and ships unrelated CI workflows, so it needs rework before merging.
